criteria.description: States that the non-streaming client receives HTTP 503 (or the upstream's actual error status code).
accept_alternatives: 5xx with explanation that proxy re-raises the upstream code

criteria.description: States that the streaming client receives HTTP 200, not 503 or any other error code.
Identifies that the two request modes produce different HTTP status codes from the same upstream error.
Explains that the non-streaming path constructs a Response object after the upstream call completes, so the error status code is available before headers are sent.
accept_alternatives: mentions that the except block at lines 201-206 returns Response with status_code=e.status_code

criteria.description: Explains that StreamingResponse sends HTTP headers (including status 200) to the client before the generator begins iterating.
accept_alternatives: mentions http.response.start is sent before body iteration
mentions that ASGI commits headers before yielding chunks

criteria.description: Identifies that the 200 status is irrevocable once sent: HTTP/1.1 does not allow changing the status code after headers are on the wire.
accept_alternatives: mentions that chunked transfer encoding commits the status with the first header block

criteria.description: Identifies that the upstream error reaches the generator as an exception (via the queue in _stream_worker, re-raised in _stream_gen).
accept_alternatives: describes the worker thread catching the exception and putting it in the queue
mentions _stream_gen re-raises exceptions from the queue

criteria.description: States that _safe_stream catches the exception and yields an SSE frame (event: error with JSON data) instead of crashing.
accept_alternatives: mentions the except block yields error content back into the stream

criteria.description: Correctly describes the error delivery format: the client receives the error as SSE content (event: error, data: JSON) within the 200 response body, not as an HTTP status code.
Does NOT claim that the streaming client receives 503. This is the primary wrong answer the rubric must reject.
Does NOT claim that the error is silently swallowed or lost. The error is delivered as SSE content.
Correctly attributes the behavior to the ASGI/Starlette response lifecycle, not to a bug or oversight in the proxy code specifically.
accept_alternatives: mentions this is inherent to how StreamingResponse works in any FastAPI app

criteria.description: Traces the error propagation path through at least three of these four stages: _stream_worker exception -> queue -> _stream_gen re-raise -> _safe_stream yield.
accept_alternatives: traces at least worker -> generator -> yield
